clue.text: Getting in a heartless nurse would be stupid

parts.note: crops that are got in are said to be in, so this phrase supplies the little word in

indicators.note: a heartless word has its middle letters cut out, leaving only its first and last letters here

explanation.surface: Admitting an incompetent nurse into the ward would be a foolish decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the inner letters of 'nurse', keeping its first and last; 'Getting in' is harvest talk, crops being in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane remarks are silly and empty, the synonym of foolish.

clue.text: The Italian soldier in the pub is unreasonable

parts.note: il is the Italian for the

indicators.note: the soldier sits inside the pub, so in marks one piece put within another

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An Italian soldier drinking in the bar is being irrational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the soldier sitting within the pub; 'local' is British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical thinking lacks sound reasoning.

clue.text: Where two sides get together to some degree

definitions.text: Where two sides get together to some degree

parts.words: Where two sides get together to some degree
parts.note: reads like a negotiation where opponents partly agree, but describes the meeting of two lines measured in degrees

explanation.surface: A compromise where two opposing parties partly meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' is a unit of measure, not an extent of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry two lines meeting at a corner form a figure measured in degrees.

clue.text: Enlarging no longer on service

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
tending is looking after or serving

explanation.surface: Someone retired from active duty is putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthening or stretching something makes it larger.

clue.text: Romans in a bad state

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Citizens of Rome find themselves living in a sorry country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the nine letters ROMANSINA; the definition is just 'state', a small independent country within Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny republic surrounded by Italy is a sovereign country, hence a state.

clue.text: Pompously crafty without dispute

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for crafty goes round the quarrel

parts.note: sly means crafty or cunning
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Pompously cunning but avoiding any argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the crafty word goes around the quarrel rather than dropping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving formally and haughtily is acting stuffily.

clue.text: Given incorrect grading, he can be very mean

indicators.note: an incorrect version of the word grading has its letters wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A student marked unfairly calls the examiner a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is stingy with money.

clue.text: A newspaper the King is following

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The monarch is reading a daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming later in time or order means coming behind.

clue.text: One does not speak well of such an isolated community

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to slander someone is to speak ill of them

explanation.surface: Gossip ostracised by a remote village.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a remote island form a cut-off community.

clue.text: A Frenchman in love with the Church — rather a lightweight

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the other pieces, so in marks a container

parts.note: O is a zero score, love in tennis
CE is the Church of England
un is how a Frenchman says a

explanation.surface: A Parisian falls for the Church, though he lacks substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Frenchman' means the word 'a' as a Frenchman says it; 'in' puts that inside love plus the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: This small unit of weight is about 28 grams, a light amount.

clue.text: "Fear no more the flash" (Cymbeline)

parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing word is the one that completes the funeral song line from Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A line from the dirge in Shakespeare's Cymbeline, with one word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank before 'flash'; the full line is 'Fear no more the ___ flash, Nor the all-dreaded thunder-stone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flash in a thunderstorm is the electrical discharge seen in the sky.

clue.text: At the end, put a pound on the remaining cards

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the next word, put

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A card player puts a pound stake on the leftover pack at the finish of a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the stock left after the deal is called by this name, also a bird's claw.

clue.text: Environmentalist signal to proceed

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner gives the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservationist is called this colour; a traffic light of the same colour means go.

clue.text: To linger in a foreign country may bring notoriety

indicators.note: the word to linger goes inside the country, so in marks one piece placed within another

parts.note: France is a foreign country from a British point of view
to lag is to trail behind or linger

explanation.surface: Overstaying abroad may get one a bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the lingering word inside the country, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrance is glaring obviousness of wrongdoing, which brings infamy.

clue.text: Confirm guarantee

explanation.surface: Two words placed side by side, each meaning to vouch for something officially.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify is both to verify formally and to vouch for something in writing.

clue.text: Check leisure includes exercise

indicators.note: the word for leisure holds the word for exercise within it

parts.note: rest is time off
to train is to exercise or practise

explanation.surface: A gym check-up shows the client's downtime includes workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a curb or holding back, as is self-control.

clue.text: Their staffs are supposed to disclose liquid assets

definitions.text: Their staffs are supposed to disclose liquid assets

parts.words: Their staffs are supposed to disclose liquid assets
parts.note: reads like company employees revealing cash holdings, but means people whose divining rods are said to find underground water

explanation.surface: Company employees are expected to reveal the firm's cash reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staffs' are rods, not employees, and 'liquid assets' are water sources rather than cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Water diviners walk with forked sticks that supposedly twitch over hidden water.

clue.text: Like a colourless milksop?

parts.note: a milksop is a weakling, and the pale face is likened to the watery part of milk

explanation.surface: Describing a pallid, feeble person.
explanation.walkthrough: The milk theme points to the watery liquid left when curds form, the colour of a pale face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pale-faced from fear or illness looks pallid.

clue.text: A personal toaster

parts.note: sounds like a private kitchen gadget, but means a person who toasts themselves in the sun

explanation.surface: A one-slice kitchen appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toaster' is not a gadget: it is someone browning themselves on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out to tan is toasting themselves.

clue.text: Food left by a sink — nauseating starters

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

indicators.note: the plural starters takes the opening pair of letters of the word nauseating

explanation.surface: A meal abandoned beside the kitchen sink, with sickening first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' here gives two letters, NA, the first two of 'nauseating', not one.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked Italian pasta dish is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Still take a drink with the doctor in charge

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Have a pint with the senior physician on duty, still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a noun here, a distilling apparatus, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: This glass vessel was used by alchemists for distilling liquids.

clue.text: A member of the family moves over

parts.note: steps are movements made on foot
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: A relative shifts along to make room.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's child from an earlier marriage is a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Sort of design clients order

indicators.note: to put in order is to rearrange, so the letters of clients are sorted anew

explanation.surface: Customers request a particular pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template is used to paint a pattern.

clue.text: School coats — always keep on!

indicators.note: the school's name wraps round the word for always, as a coat covers a body

parts.note: the Perse School is a well-known independent school in Cambridge
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A headteacher's rallying cry about school blazers: never give up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' means the school's name wraps round the word for always; the Perse is an independent school in Cambridge, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist means carrying on despite difficulty.

clue.text: Sue newspapers

explanation.surface: Taking the papers to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to urge or petition, as in pressing a claim; the press is the newspaper industry.

clue.text: Individual dining in a brasserie — a terrible place

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A lone diner in an awful restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the final E of brasserie into A and TER of terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone having a meal is consuming food.

clue.text: A girl's bloomers!

explanation.surface: A young woman's knickers!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear but means things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, and also the plant life of a region, things that blossom.

clue.text: Ring the sector supplying the gas

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a zone is a sector or area

explanation.surface: Call the district that provides the gas supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms is a gas in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: The law reform cited

indicators.note: to reform is to shape again, so the five letters of cited are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judicial change was quoted in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by an authority has the force of law.

clue.text: Favour ministers setting the scene for the players

definitions.text: setting the scene for the players

parts.note: to back someone is to support or favour them
the cloth is a collective term for clergy

explanation.surface: Supporting clergy are present while the actors prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted curtain hung at the rear of a stage provides scenery for actors.

clue.text: It's racial in origin — that's critical

indicators.note: the words it's racial are taken back to raw material and remade, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something rooted in race is a sensitive matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in origin' asks for the letters of IT'S RACIAL to be reworked; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, scathing commentary is fault-finding in tone.

clue.text: Gloomy note put to the back

parts.note: D is a note in the musical scale
the rear is the back part of something

explanation.surface: A depressing memo pinned up at the rear of the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal.
